evaluation.final_reason: The parties reached concrete, mutual arrangements: Agent A agreed to ventilation and to allow D two late-week stove slots or accept requests for extra portions conditional on chip-in or swaps: "You can have two late-week slots each week. These concrete, mutual commitments settled the substantive incompatibilities.

substantive_insights: Three separate but related problems (smell/ventilation, unwashed dishes, and stove access) required distinct solutions; the group addressed each with a targeted commitment rather than a single blanket rule.
Practical scheduling (stove slots) can be resolved by allocating fixed times plus a conditional mechanism (request + chip-in/swap) to handle ad hoc needs.
Assigning responsibility for shared supplies ($10/month, rotating purchaser) and an explicit first volunteer (B) reduced ambiguity about ongoing chores/costs.
